title: Regular closed points over an algebraically closed field are smooth (proved source theorem)
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $A$ a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and $q$ a maximal ideal of $A$. If $A_q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], then $A$ is smooth over $k$ at $q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00TV (lemma-separable-smooth), regular implies smooth, at a closed point with residue field k; equivalently Lemma 00TS (lemma-finite-type-algebraically-closed), (1) implies (4). Source-library implementation: WeilConjectures/Mathlib/RingTheory/Smooth/Local.lean:51-193 and 226-235.

proof.text: The already proved source theorem Algebra.IsSmoothAt.of_isRegularLocalRing_of_isAlgClosed is the exact statement. Its proof makes the residue field finite over k using Zariski's lemma and then identifies it with k by algebraic closedness. Thus its algebra map is surjective and the residue field is formally smooth over k.

The source proof localizes a finite polynomial presentation at the prime above q. This gives a surjection from a regular local formally smooth polynomial localization B to A_q. Apply the proved regular-local-quotient independent-generators theorem to its kernel. The cotangent map to the differential fibre is injective because the residue field is formally smooth. The kernel generators therefore have independent differential images. The source proves injectivity of the cotangent-complex base-change map by expressing its elements as linear combinations of these generators and using their independence. Mathlib Algebra.FormallySmooth.iff_injective_cotangentComplexBaseChange proves formal smoothness of A_q, which is IsSmoothAt k q.
